section: Social Studies · Ch48 — Indian & World Geography
subject: Social Studies
stem: Which is the largest continent by both area and population?
explanation: Asia is the largest continent by both area and population. Africa is the second-largest by area; Europe and North America are considerably smaller.

section: Social Studies · Ch48 — Indian & World Geography
subject: Social Studies
stem: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
explanation: Gujarat has India's longest coastline (~1,600 km) among states. Andhra Pradesh has the second-longest coastline among Indian states.

section: Social Studies · Ch48 — Indian & World Geography
subject: Social Studies
stem: Tropical evergreen forests, found in regions with over 200 cm of annual rainfall (e.g. parts of the Western Ghats and North-East India), are characterised by:

options.option_text: Dense, multi-layered canopy of trees that do not shed leaves together in any season
Short thorny scrub adapted to very low rainfall
Trees that shed all their leaves together in a fixed season
Absence of any tree cover, only grassland

explanation: Tropical evergreen forests get abundant, well-distributed rainfall and remain green year-round with a dense multi-layer canopy — contrasting with deciduous forests (seasonal leaf-shedding) and thorny scrub (arid regions).

section: Social Studies · Ch51 — Economics: Basic Concepts
subject: Social Studies
stem: The total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given year is called:
explanation: GDP measures the value of final goods/services produced domestically in a year. Per capita income divides national income by population; fiscal deficit is the excess of government spending over revenue.

section: Social Studies · Ch51 — Economics: Basic Concepts
subject: Social Studies
stem: Agriculture, fishing and mining — activities directly extracting or producing from natural resources — together belong to which sector of the economy?
explanation: The primary sector directly draws from nature (agriculture, fishing, mining). The secondary sector processes/manufactures those raw materials (industry); the tertiary sector provides services (banking, education, transport).
